Enel SpA Names New Chief Operating Officer Amid Strategic Expansion

ROME—Enel SpA, Italy’s largest electric utilities company, announced on Monday the appointment of Paola Bianchi as its new Chief Operating Officer, effective July 1. The move comes as Enel continues to pursue its multi-year strategy focused on digitalization, grid modernization, and renewable energy integration.

Bianchi, who has served as Enel’s Head of Network Operations since 2020, brings over two decades of experience in energy infrastructure and operational management. She succeeds Marco Leone, who is retiring after a 37-year career at the company.

“We are delighted to welcome Paola to the executive team in this critical role,” said Enel CEO Giovanni Ferraro in a statement. “Her proven leadership and deep technical expertise will be instrumental as we accelerate our efforts to create a more resilient and sustainable energy system.”

The appointment comes at a time of significant investment for Enel SpA, which reported capital expenditures of €9.4 billion in 2023, a 6% increase from the previous year. The company is expanding its renewables portfolio and upgrading its distribution networks across Italy and key international markets.

Analysts view the leadership transition as a sign of continuity with Enel’s long-term objectives. “Bianchi’s track record in project execution and digital innovation aligns with Enel’s focus on efficiency and growth,” said Carlo Venturi, an energy sector analyst at Milani & Partners. “Her appointment is likely to reassure both investors and employees that the company’s transformation is on course.”

Enel SpA employs more than 66,000 people worldwide and serves over 75 million end users. In Italy, its modernization efforts have included the installation of over 13 million smart meters and the launch of new customer-focused digital platforms.

Union representatives welcomed the announcement, noting Bianchi’s collaborative approach. “Paola has engaged constructively with workers and their representatives, particularly during the rollout of new grid technologies,” said Lucia Romano of the Federenergia labor union.

Bianchi issued a brief statement, emphasizing her commitment to operational excellence and sustainability. “I am honored to take on this responsibility at a pivotal moment for Enel and the broader energy transition,” she said. “Together, we will continue to deliver reliable power and innovate for a clean energy future.”
